boundary: The Azuero-Soná fault rupture (left-lateral, WNW-ESE). In this NISAR frame the coherent ground north of the fault shows huge LOS motion (+60 to +170 cm on the Tonosí plain and the hills to its NW). South of it is a decorrelated, landslide-scarred band (coherence <0.1, no valid pixels) running roughly from the SW corner past 7.42–7.46°N to the coast between Búcaro and Isla Cañas. At Búcaro's longitude the LOS drops about 60 cm across that band: +75–82 cm at 7.42°N vs +17 cm at Búcaro on the coast. Field teams measured 1–1.2 m of horizontal and about 1 m of vertical surface rupture at Búcaro.

items.title: Búcaro: the ground split 1–1.2 m sideways and 1 m up; the road 'lifted two to three metres'
items.place: Búcaro fishing village, Tonosí district, Los Santos
items.what_it_shows: Senacyt doctoral researcher Isaac Guerra Araúz measured surface rupture at Búcaro: 1–1.2 m horizontal and about 1 m vertical (La Estrella, citing Senacyt). La Prensa (29 Oct): resident Jairo Araújo Jiménez describes the house moving 'like a wave', the hillside sliding, a wave reaching the point, and fleeing along a split road raised 2–3 m in places. OCHA SitRep 3: many homes destroyed and residents camped at the village entrance.
items.credit: La Prensa (Panamá), photos Alexander Arosemena; La Estrella de Panamá https://www.laestrella.com.pa/panama/nacional/terremoto-hundio-30-centimetros-de-isla-canas-de-acuerdo-a-estudios-preliminares-MB26639225; OCHA SitRep 3 https://reliefweb.int/report/panama/panama-earthquake-azuero-veraguas-situation-report-no-03-12-october-2026-1430
items.notes: Village coordinates are from GeoNames 3713745 (via geoview.info); Búcaro is not in OSM. The exact rupture crossing within or near the village is not published, so the location is good to about 0.5–1 km. Telemetro also reports a 70 m long, 4 m deep collapse of the only access road at El Pital: https://www.telemetro.com/nacionales/carretera-bucaro-los-santos-colapsa-y-pone-riesgo-conductores-n6094962

items.title: Tonosí: hotel collapsed; patients treated in tents
items.what_it_shows: en.wikipedia: 'A hotel and several homes collapsed in Tonosí.' TVN: owner Rosendo describes the collapse of Hotel Mi Valle (two people inside got out unhurt). OCHA: 11 townships without water or power. Public-domain US Army photo: Panamanian medics working in a US-provided tent in Tonosí, 19 Oct.
items.credit: U.S. Army photo by Pfc. Carolyn Dodge (Commons); TVN https://www.tvn-2.com/nacionales/temblor-panama-tonosi-enfrenta-perdidas_1_2266543.html
items.notes: The point is the OSM town node; Hospital Rural de Tonosí is at 7.41015,-80.43758, ~150 m away and the likely site of the tent, but the photo caption does not name it. No address was found for Hotel Mi Valle.

items.title: El Cacao: a resident in front of his earthquake-damaged home
items.place: El Cacao village, Tonosí district, Los Santos
items.what_it_shows: World Central Kitchen photo: 'A resident of El Cacao stands in front of his home, damaged by the earthquake.' Companion photos show children receiving meals.
items.credit: World Central Kitchen (Flickr) via Wikimedia Commons
items.notes: There are two places called El Cacao: El Cacao, Veraguas (outside the frame) and El Cacao, Tonosí. This photo is filed under Category:Tonosí District on Commons, so it is taken to be the Tonosí village (OSM node). Which house in the village is not known.

items.title: Isla Cañas sank 15–30 cm and was cut in two by the sea
items.place: Isla Cañas (village), Tonosí district, Los Santos
items.what_it_shows: La Estrella (Senacyt): preliminary 15–30 cm subsidence at Isla Cañas plus seabed deformation. es.wikipedia/Telemetro: the island was split in two by a channel. La Prensa: residents Gabriel Aguirre and Jorge Ríos on flooded farmland and whether to return. About 300 people evacuated on 9 Oct for fear of a tsunami.
items.credit: La Estrella de Panamá; La Prensa (Ohigginis Arcia Jaramillo)
items.notes: Village from OSM (Isla Cañas place=village). The island centroid is at 7.40397,-80.32638. Exactly where the breach is was not established.

items.title: Macaracas: a 68-year-old woman killed by a collapsing wall, far from the rupture
items.what_it_shows: en.wikipedia: 'A 68 year-old woman was seriously injured and later died of her injuries due to a collapsing wall in Macaracas.' One of the three deaths.
items.notes: Only the town is known (OSM town node), so the location is good to about 1 km. Use it as a far-side contrast rather than a pinpoint.

items.title: Río Oria bridge closed: residents carry supplies across on foot
items.place: Bridge over Río Oria near Oria Arriba, Pedasí district, Los Santos (road to Tonosí)
items.what_it_shows: Telemetro: the bridge over the Río Oria in Pedasí district stays closed with slab damage, so residents cross on foot carrying belongings and supplies. OCHA SitRep 3 also lists the Oria bridge closure cutting road access to Tonosí.
items.notes: The coordinates are the OSM node for Oria Arriba village. The bridge is where the Pedasí–Tonosí road crosses the Río Oria nearby, but it was not located exactly, so the position could be off by 1–2 km.

items.title: Las Tablas: the provincial hospital stayed fit to treat patients while Tonosí's was shut
items.place: Hospital Joaquín Pablo Franco Sayas, Las Tablas, Los Santos
items.what_it_shows: TVN, 14 Oct: Health Minister Fernando Boyd Galindo said 68 of Minsa's 842 facilities were affected, but 'el Hospital Aquilino Tejeira, Cecilio Castillero y Joaquín Pablo Franco, están en condiciones de atender a nuestra gente'; checks were of floor tiles and ceilings. The same report names Tonosí's hospital as one of the most compromised. OPS/OMS (15 Oct) found the Hospital Rural de Tonosí out of service with significant structural damage, about 45 km SW, while its mission went on to visit the Las Tablas hospital.
items.notes: The hospital was not untouched. A Telemetro headline on 11 Oct reports tents set up at the hospital to see patients (article not retrieved), and on the first night people from Las Tablas slept in the Roberto 'Flaco Bala' Hernández stadium for fear of aftershocks (Telemetro headline, 10 Oct). Damaged homes are reported in and around the town, e.g. 223 at La Enea de Guararé, 9 km NW. So 'unaffected' is relative: the building stayed usable while Tonosí's did not. Location is the OSM hospital (Hospital Joaquín Pablo Franco), good to about 100 m.

items.title: Cañas: the mainland village took in the families from the island that sank
items.place: Cañas village, Tonosí district, Los Santos (mainland, about 6 km NE of Isla Cañas)
items.what_it_shows: OPS/OMS, 15 Oct: 'En Cañas se alojan familias desplazadas de Isla Cañas', in tents, with water pooling around some of them. Isla Cañas itself sank 15–30 cm and was cut in two (panama-04); the mainland village a few kilometres away was where its people were sheltered.
items.notes: Evidence is indirect: being a shelter site implies the village was usable, not that it was undamaged. PAHO notes rural aqueducts in the area were affected, and a Metro Libre headline (9 Nov) says the M5.9 aftershock of 31 Oct left Cañas without power. NISAR here is not entirely quiet (local step ~7 cm, coherence ~0.4). Isla de Cañas is a separate corregimiento, so 'Cañas' is read as the mainland village. Location is the OSM village node; the camp itself was not located.

items.title: Cambutal: across the fault from Tonosí, considered as a place to move Tonosí's patients
items.place: Cambutal village, Tonosí district, Los Santos (Pacific coast, south of the rupture)
items.what_it_shows: TVN, 14 Oct, quoting the health minister: Tonosí's hospital, which sees more than 100 people a day, is one of the most compromised, and Minsa 'contempla trasladar parte de la atención hacia Cambutal'. That points to Cambutal's health post still being usable, about 17 km SSW of Tonosí on the other side of the rupture.
items.notes: A plan to move care there is the only evidence found; no report describes Cambutal's own damage either way. Treat it as a lead, not a finding. Location is the OSM village node; the health post (reopened 2012 per Telemetro) was not located.
